messages.subject: Functions as reactive conductors
parts:
Hi,

This is a post in response to the article on Reactivity:

shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reactivity-overview.html

I read this article in detail before trying to implement a conductor (to speed up my calculations by only doing them once).
I initially tried to set up the code in the way specified in the code example just above the Summary section:
"On the other hand, if currentFib is a function that accesses a reactive value, and that function is called within the reactive world, then it will work:"

This did not work; the calculations still ended up being re-run every time. Even though the function was being called by renderPlot and by renderText, as in the example above, and the function itself was calling the reactive elements.

When I changed by calculation from a function to a reactive element, then everything worked.
So my problem is not that the reactivity didn't work, but that the alternative example you gave that should have also worked, did not work.
The *only* thing I changed was to change the calculations from a function into a reactive element.

My app is https://lmcm177.shinyapps.io/genechart-upload

I don't know whether there are other things I needed to do to get run_geneplot_calcs to work as a function instead of as a reactive, but the reactivity didn't work when it was a function. So it would be helpful if you either removed that example from the article, or explained why it might not have worked as an alternative to a reactive element.

Thanks,

Louise
